tweets: Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram: the Char Dham, four shrines at India's north, west, east and south, said to have been bound into one pilgrim circuit by the 8th-century sage Ādi Śaṅkara — a single sacred geography spanning the length of the subcontinent.

Each dham enshrines a distinct form of the divine: Viṣṇu at snow-bound Badrinath, Kṛṣṇa at Dwarka, Jagannātha's wood image at Puri, a Śiva liṅga at Rāmeśwaram where Rāma is said to have worshipped before crossing to Laṅkā. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
